title: Reason Code 48 — no network policy matched
plain_english: Authentication may even have been possible — but the connection attempt fell through every network policy without matching one, so NPS rejected it by default. The event tells you who tried; your policy conditions tell you why none of them claimed the request.

any: did not match any network policy

causes.cause: The user or computer isn't in the AD group your policy uses as a condition — or the policy checks 'User Groups' while the device does machine auth (computer object), or vice versa.
causes.next_check: Check the account named in this event against the policy's group condition — and confirm the object type matches (user vs computer). Nested-group and cross-domain memberships are frequent traps.

causes.cause: A condition like NAS Port Type doesn't match what the NAS sends — e.g. policy requires 'Wireless - IEEE 802.11' but the controller sends 'Ethernet'.
causes.next_check: Compare the NAS Port Type / other RADIUS attributes in this event with each condition of the policy you expected to match.

causes.cause: Policy ordering: a broader policy above the intended one grabs (and rejects) the request, or the intended policy is disabled.
causes.next_check: In the NPS console, review policy order top-to-bottom with this event's attributes in hand — the first match wins.
